clue.text: Heed secretary initially desiring thing for scribbling

parts.note: to heed something is to note it
PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: initially points to the start of a word, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An office instruction to attend to a secretary who keeps wanting something to doodle on.
explanation.walkthrough: PA, short for personal assistant, is the standard crossword secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pad of paper is the everyday object used for jotting quick written reminders.

clue.text: Subtle detail in French city today at the margins

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

indicators.note: margins are the edges of a page, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A traveller noticing some fine point in a French city on a particular day.
explanation.walkthrough: The city's name is spelt like the English adjective, which helps the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine distinction or precise point, the kind of small refinement easily overlooked.

clue.text: Swimmer skirts river channel?

indicators.note: to skirt is to run around the edge, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A swimmer keeping close to the bank of a river or channel.
explanation.walkthrough: A swimmer in crosswords is usually a fish; here the tench, a European pond fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch dug in the ground, which can carry water like a channel.

clue.text: In other words, soldier over period accepting a right

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase defining a noun or verb: a paraphrase puts something in other words

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece receives another inside it

parts.note: a phase is a period or stage
R is the abbreviation for right, here one right

explanation.surface: A sentence describing a soldier serving a stretch of duty and claiming an entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the soldier above the rest; PHASE then takes in a single R.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphrasing means restating a passage using different wording while keeping its meaning, which is what saying it in other words does.

clue.text: Dorothy hoards old record in storage site

indicators.note: to hoard is to store something away, so one piece is kept inside another

parts.note: Dot is a short form of Dorothy
an EP, extended play, is an old vinyl record format

explanation.surface: Dorothy stashes a vintage record in a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Short names are a crossword staple: Dorothy becomes DOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a warehouse or yard where goods or vehicles are kept until needed.

clue.text: Cop, say, getting agitated about last part of controversial Caribbean song

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround another
something agitated is stirred and shaken, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material

indicators.note: the last part of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A policeman getting worked up about the closing verse of a provocative song from the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cop, say' reads as a policeman as an example, but it is just six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is a style of rhythmic, often satirical music from Trinidad and the wider West Indies.

clue.text: Preserve a form of service in honour of noted artist

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it
taken as written
in tennis a let is a serve that must be replayed
a dedication 'to' someone honours them

explanation.surface: Keeping alive a type of church service to honour a famous painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests church, but it is a tennis serve; a let is replayed when the ball clips the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was the eighteenth-century Venetian painter famed for detailed city views of Venice and London.

clue.text: Lieutenant, appearing about middle of film, has a pleasing accent

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece shows up wrapped around another

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters

parts.note: the two central letters of the word

explanation.surface: An officer who turns up halfway through a movie speaks with a charming voice.
explanation.walkthrough: A four-letter word has a two-letter middle, so both central letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A lilt is the gentle rising and falling rhythm in a voice, often heard as a pleasant regional way of speaking.

clue.text: No amateur, Welsh footballer pockets first of bonuses? That's likely

parts.note: the opposite of an amateur is a professional

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Gareth Bale is a famous Welsh footballer

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A professional Welsh player collecting extra payments seems all too plausible.
explanation.walkthrough: Gareth Bale played for Real Madrid and captained Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that will probably happen, an outcome with a good chance of being true.

clue.text: Telephone connection in US city on reflection is a joke!

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Reno is a city in Nevada
a phone line connects callers

explanation.surface: Getting a phone line in some American city turns out to be laughable.
explanation.walkthrough: The city runs backwards to ONER, and the phone link sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a short quip or gag delivered in a single sentence, a brief witty remark.

clue.text: Chapter by English poet is easy to understand

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for chapter
Edward Lear was an English poet of nonsense verse

explanation.surface: A section written by an English poet is accessible to readers.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear wrote The Owl and the Pussy-cat; crosswords use him often.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear is plain and lucid, so its meaning can be grasped without difficulty.

clue.text: Leaden cop messed up a means of controlling crime

indicators.note: something messed up has been thrown into disorder, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material

explanation.surface: A sluggish policeman bungles the job of fighting crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The policing surface hides that all nine letters of the first two words are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A penal code is the body of laws setting out offences and punishments, a system for restraining criminal behaviour.

clue.text: Retired group touring Paris, perhaps as a climax

indicators.note: a tour goes all the way around somewhere, so one piece encircles another
to retire is to go back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch
Paris is an example of a capital city

explanation.surface: A party of pensioners on a tour of Paris saving the best for last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris, perhaps' is a definition by example; the 'perhaps' warns that Paris stands for the class it belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces the final and most striking item in a series, the culmination or crowning event.

clue.text: Part of formal inspectorate in here in Africa

indicators.note: a part of a phrase is a run of letters inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Some branch of an official inspection body operating locally in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here in Africa' defines by pointing: a place found in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked West African country, so it is a place located on that continent.

clue.text: Flip over comic performer given large reptile

parts.note: a turn is a performer or act in a variety show
a turtle is a reptile, some species very large

explanation.surface: A comedian is handed a big lizard and does a somersault.
explanation.walkthrough: In British variety theatre a 'turn' is a single act on the bill, often a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn turtle is an idiom for capsizing, as a boat ends up upside down like an overturned shell.

clue.text: Artist much appreciated struggle by the French to defend refined dish of theirs

indicators.note: to defend is to surround and protect, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
ta is British slang for thanks
to toil is to struggle
U means upper class, hence refined
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A celebrated painter battles alongside the French to protect their sophisticated cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ta' is British for thank you; U is an old label for upper-class usage. 'Theirs' points back to the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratatouille is a Provençal vegetable stew, so it is a dish belonging to French cooking.

clue.text: Crude lies about unorthodox set beginning to suffer

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: tales can be lies, as in telling tales

indicators.note: unorthodox means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Vulgar falsehoods about an eccentric crowd begin to cause harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' sits first and looks like it describes the lies, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crude joke lacks refinement or decency, which is exactly what calling something vulgar and in poor taste means.

clue.text: Pointer initially ignored by soldiers and worker? That's ill-mannered

indicators.note: ignoring the initial means dropping the opening letter

parts.note: a sign points the way
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A dog left unnoticed by troops and a labourer feels slighted by their rudeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointer' suggests the dog breed, but it is a signpost.
explanation.definitionFit: In British colloquial use an ignorant person is rude or discourteous, not just lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Something that might be laid on two men in short showing bad faith

definitions.note: a phrase describing the act, defining a noun

parts.note: a bet is laid on a horse
Ray and Al, Al being short for Albert or Alan

explanation.surface: A wager placed on a pair of men, briefly, turns out to be a double-cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid' sounds like laying a table, but bets are laid.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal is treachery, the breaking of trust or loyalty owed to someone.

clue.text: Go with person, say, after work to find cheap cafe

indicators.note: once letters have been worked on they are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material
taken as written as anagram material

explanation.surface: Heading off with a colleague after a shift to grab food at a budget diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person, say' reads like a definition by example, but every letter is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A greasy spoon is British slang for a cheap, unpretentious cafe serving fried breakfasts.

clue.text: British trio's refurbished inexpensive eatery

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British

indicators.note: something refurbished has been made over, so its letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Three Britons have done up a modest little restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is surface dressing; only the letters of 'trios' are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant serving simple, moderately priced meals.

clue.text: Soviet leader left in sign of disgrace

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a stain on one's character marks disgrace
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A Soviet ruler departed leaving a lasting mark of shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed but gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin ruled the Soviet Union from the 1920s until his death in 1953.

clue.text: Right-winger in Barking breaking valuable material is monstrous type

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it

parts.note: ore is rock from which valuable metal is extracted

indicators.note: the right wing of a word is its rightmost end, its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A right-wing politician in Barking smashing up precious goods is a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right-winger' looks political, but it means the right-hand end of the next word. Barking is a district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, and by extension any cruel, frightening person.

clue.text: Foot expert is pictured at work

indicators.note: letters at work are being worked over, so they are reordered

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material

explanation.surface: A podiatrist is photographed while on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is so natural that 'at work' passes as description rather than a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicurist treats and cares for people's feet and toenails, a specialist in foot care.

clue.text: Perfect introduction by a croupier?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: flawless, as good as can be
second meaning: how a dealer of cards might introduce himself, split as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as 'I deal' and it is what a croupier, who deals at a casino table, might say of their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ideal satisfies every wish and could not be improved on, so it is flawless.

clue.text: Attractive cruet set seen every now and again

indicators.note: something seen only now and again shows up at intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A pretty salt-and-pepper set that only occasionally appears on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: A cruet set holds salt, pepper and condiments at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means charming or pretty in an endearing way, so it is a near synonym.

clue.text: Description of second person's past military command?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read literally, a phrase describing how 'you' used to be
second meaning: the order telling soldiers to return to their previous position

explanation.walkthrough: 'Second person' is grammar: 'you', and its past tense of 'are' is 'were'.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill order cancels a previous instruction, telling troops to resume their former stance.

clue.text: Small drink obtained before a litre as full amount

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
taken as written
L is the symbol for litre

explanation.surface: A little nip taken before downing a whole litre, as the complete quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places the drink ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the whole sum when everything has been added together, the complete quantity.

clue.text: One trailing first to last conversationalists

indicators.note: moving the first to the end shifts the opening letter to the back

parts.note: a stalker trails someone

explanation.surface: Someone following the leader all the way to the end of the chatty crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailing' looks like lagging behind, but it means following someone covertly.
explanation.definitionFit: Conversationalists are people who chat, so those who talk a lot are simply talkers.

clue.text: Now idle, adjusted to a spell in retirement?

indicators.note: something adjusted has been rearranged, so its letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material

explanation.surface: A newly idle worker settles into a period of retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests ending work, but it also means going to bed; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-down is a short rest lying flat, a brief nap taken after retiring to bed or sofa.
